1	/**
2	 * Northgate Family Medicine — chart event log, version 1.
3	 *
4	 * Northgate is a primary-care practice. Its EHR keeps the chart as an append-only log of small
5	 * events, and publishes each event as one FOLIO record item: one signed visit note, one vital-sign
6	 * set, one medication change, one problem-list change, one allergy-list change, one list review,
7	 * one interfaced lab result report, one referral step, or one void.
8	 *
9	 * Most items carry exactly one payload entry. Three kinds carry several: an imported result report has
10	 * one entry per result component (a renal panel has a creatinine entry and one or more eGFR entries); a
11	 * signed visit note has its `visit` entry plus one `billing_dx` entry per billed diagnosis; a referral
12	 * step has its `referral_event` entry plus one `referral_dx` entry per diagnosis on the referral.
13	 * Diagnoses are separate entries, never lists inside another entry, so a patient can share a visit note
14	 * or referral while withholding one diagnosis (for example a behavioral-health code).
15	 *
16	 * There is no "current state" record. The current medication list, problem list and allergy list
17	 * are what you get by replaying the events in `effective` order for each list-line id (`med_id`,
18	 * `problem_id`, `allergy_id`), after dropping items that were retracted or superseded.
19	 *
20	 * Conventions that apply to every entry type:
21	 * - Times carry an offset. Northgate is in America/Chicago (-06:00 standard, -05:00 daylight).
22	 * - Item narrative is what the clinician typed into the event's comment box or signed as a note.
23	 *   It is never generated from the payload. Many items have no narrative.
24	 * - `visit_id`, where present, is Northgate's visit number (e.g. "V-2024-111203"). It groups the
25	 *   events entered during one visit. Absent for events entered outside a visit (interfaced
26	 *   results, phone refills, chart corrections).
27	 * - Items received through the lab interface have no `author`; every other item's author is the
28	 *   Northgate user who entered it.
29	 */
30	
31	/** One entry in a Northgate item. Discriminated by `type`. */
32	export type ChartEvent =
33	  | Visit
34	  | VitalSet
35	  | MedEvent
36	  | ProblemEvent
37	  | AllergyEvent
38	  | BillingDx
39	  | ListReviewed
40	  | ImportedResult
41	  | ReferralEvent
42	  | ReferralDx
43	  | ChartCorrection;
44	
45	/**
46	 * Restricted-chart category. Northgate hides restricted entries from users without the matching
47	 * privilege and excludes them from routine outbound records unless the patient consents.
48	 * - 'BH': behavioral health (depression, anxiety, and the medications used for them).
49	 * Absent means not restricted. The flag is set by the clinician when the entry is created and
50	 * restated on every later event for the same list line.
51	 */
52	export type Restriction = 'BH';
53	
54	/**
55	 * A full date (`YYYY-MM-DD`) with how much of it is real. Northgate's date picker always stores a
56	 * full date; when the clinician knows only the year or month, it fills the rest with 01 and records
57	 * the precision. So `{ date: "2016-01-01", precision: "year" }` means "sometime in 2016", not
58	 * January 1st.
59	 */
60	export interface FuzzyDate {
61	  /** Always a full date. Days and months beyond `precision` are filler (`01`). */
62	  date: string;
63	  /**
64	   * How much of `date` is meaningful.
65	   * - 'year': only the year is known.
66	   * - 'month': year and month are known.
67	   * - 'day': the full date is known.
68	   */
69	  precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day';
70	}
71	
72	/**
73	 * A visit note: the clinician's signed note for one office, telehealth or nurse visit. The item
74	 * narrative is the note itself, which is usually a few terse lines. The visit's billing diagnoses are
75	 * `billing_dx` entries in the same item. The structured events from the same visit (vitals, medication
76	 * and problem changes) are separate items sharing the `visit_id`.
77	 */
78	export interface Visit {
79	  type: 'visit';
80	
81	  /** Northgate visit number. Stable; every event entered during this visit carries it. */
82	  visit_id: string;
83	
84	  /**
85	   * Kind of visit.
86	   * - 'office': in-person visit with a clinician.
87	   * - 'telehealth': video visit.
88	   * - 'nurse': nurse-only visit (BP check, injection teaching). No clinician exam.
89	   * - 'phone': documented phone encounter.
90	   */
91	  visit_type: 'office' | 'telehealth' | 'nurse' | 'phone';
92	
93	  /** Reason for visit as typed at scheduling or check-in, e.g. "Hosp f/u". Free text. */
94	  reason: string;
95	}
96	
97	/**
98	 * One billing diagnosis of a visit, in the visit note's item (one entry per code). These are what was
99	 * billed, not the problem list: a code here does not add, change or confirm a problem. Follow-up and
100	 * screening codes (Z codes) appear here and never on the problem list.
101	 */
102	export interface BillingDx {
103	  type: 'billing_dx';
104	
105	  /** The visit billed (the `visit` entry in the same item). */
106	  visit_id: string;
107	
108	  /** Position on the claim, 1 = primary. */
109	  rank: number;
110	
111	  /** ICD-10-CM code, with the dot. */
112	  icd10cm: string;
113	
114	  /** Northgate's display text for the code. */
115	  display: string;
116	
117	  /** Restricted-chart category; see `Restriction`. Set on behavioral-health codes. */
118	  restricted?: Restriction;
119	}
120	
121	/**
122	 * One set of vital signs taken together, usually by a medical assistant at check-in. Any member
123	 * may be absent when it was not measured. Values are as entered on the flowsheet; nothing is
124	 * derived (BMI is not stored).
125	 */
126	export interface VitalSet {
127	  type: 'vital_set';
128	
129	  /** Visit the set was taken at. Absent for a stand-alone BP check logged outside a visit. */
130	  visit_id?: string;
131	
132	  /**
133	   * Blood pressure as typed on the flowsheet: text "systolic/diastolic" in mmHg, e.g. "152/94".
134	   * Always two integers separated by "/". Absent if not taken.
135	   */
136	  bp?: string;
137	
138	  /**
139	   * A second blood pressure taken later in the same visit, same text form as `bp`. Present only
140	   * when the first was high and the MA repeated it. Both readings are valid measurements.
141	   */
142	  bp_repeat?: string;
143	
144	  /**
145	   * Patient position for `bp` and `bp_repeat`.
146	   * - 'sitting', 'standing', 'supine': as recorded. Absent means not recorded (almost always sitting).
147	   */
148	  bp_position?: 'sitting' | 'standing' | 'supine';
149	
150	  /** Pulse, beats per minute. */
151	  pulse_bpm?: number;
152	
153	  /** Weight in pounds, clothed, clinic scale. One decimal place. */
154	  weight_lb?: number;
155	
156	  /** Height in inches. Usually measured once a year; absent otherwise. */
157	  height_in?: number;
158	
159	  /** Oral temperature, degrees Fahrenheit. */
160	  temp_f?: number;
161	
162	  /** Pulse oximetry, percent, room air. */
163	  spo2_pct?: number;
164	}
165	
166	/**
167	 * One change to one line of the medication list: started, dose changed, held, resumed, stopped,
168	 * or added from an outside record. Every event restates the whole order line as it stands after
169	 * the event (on a 'stop' or 'hold', the line as it was when stopped or held), so a single event is
170	 * readable on its own.
171	 */
172	export interface MedEvent {
173	  type: 'med_event';
174	
175	  /**
176	   * Northgate medication-list line id, e.g. "ML-30418". Stable across all events for one line.
177	   * A drug that is stopped and later restarted gets a new line id.
178	   */
179	  med_id: string;
180	
181	  /**
182	   * What happened to the line.
183	   * - 'start': line created; the patient should start (or, for medications already taken at the
184	   *   first Northgate visit, is already taking) the drug.
185	   * - 'change': dose, frequency or sig changed; the line stays active.
186	   * - 'hold': paused with intent to resume. The line stays on Northgate's list, shown "On hold";
187	   *   the patient should not be taking it. A hold does not expire on its own: it lasts until a
188	   *   'resume' or 'stop' event, however long that takes.
189	   * - 'resume': a held line is active again.
190	   * - 'stop': discontinued. Final for this line; a restart is a new 'start' with a new `med_id`.
191	   * Held is not stopped and not active. Only the latest event per `med_id` says where a line stands.
192	   */
193	  action: 'start' | 'change' | 'hold' | 'resume' | 'stop';
194	
195	  /**
196	   * Where the line came from.
197	   * - 'northgate': prescribed or managed by a Northgate clinician.
198	   * - 'outside': entered during medication reconciliation from another organization's record
199	   *   (e.g. a Lakeview nephrology visit summary). Northgate does not manage it and learns of
200	   *   changes only when someone reconciles again, so outside lines can lag the prescriber's record.
201	   */
202	  origin: 'northgate' | 'outside';
203	
204	  /**
205	   * The drug.
206	   * - `name`: display name as on the order, e.g. "losartan 50 MG Oral Tablet".
207	   * - `rxnorm`: RxNorm CUI (SCD or SBD) from Northgate's drug file. Present for Northgate-prescribed
208	   *   lines; often absent for 'outside' lines, which carry only `outside_code`.
209	   * - `outside_code`: the other organization's drug identifier as it appeared in their record,
210	   *   with `system` naming that organization's code space (e.g. "lakeview-drug"). Present only on
211	   *   'outside' lines. Not mapped to RxNorm.
212	   */
213	  drug: {
214	    name: string;
215	    rxnorm?: string;
216	    outside_code?: { system: string; code: string };
217	  };
218	
219	  /**
220	   * Amount per dose. `unit` is Northgate's dose unit text: "mg", "units" (insulin), or "tab".
221	   * Absent when the sig cannot be expressed as one amount (e.g. sliding scale).
222	   */
223	  dose?: { value: number; unit: string };
224	
225	  /**
226	   * Northgate frequency code.
227	   * - 'QD': once daily. 'BID': twice daily. 'TID': three times daily.
228	   * - 'QHS': once daily at bedtime. 'PRN': as needed. 'OTHER': see `sig`.
229	   */
230	  frequency?: 'QD' | 'BID' | 'TID' | 'QHS' | 'PRN' | 'OTHER';
231	
232	  /** Patient instructions exactly as printed on the prescription, e.g. "Take 1 tablet by mouth daily". */
233	  sig?: string;
234	
235	  /**
236	   * Why the line was stopped. Present on every 'stop'; absent on other actions.
237	   * - 'adverse_reaction': stopped because of a side effect or adverse reaction. A matching
238	   *   allergy-list event (`allergy_event`) is usually entered the same day, but not always.
239	   * - 'ineffective': not working well enough.
240	   * - 'therapy_changed': replaced by a different drug for the same purpose.
241	   * - 'course_complete': finite course finished.
242	   * - 'patient_choice': patient declined to continue.
243	   * - 'other': see `reason_text`.
244	   */
245	  stop_reason?: 'adverse_reaction' | 'ineffective' | 'therapy_changed' | 'course_complete' | 'patient_choice' | 'other';
246	
247	  /** Clinician's free-text reason for this event. Common on 'stop', 'hold' and 'change'; rare on 'start'. */
248	  reason_text?: string;
249	
250	  /**
251	   * On 'hold' only: the date the prescriber plans to review the hold. A planning date, not an
252	   * automatic resume; absent when no date was given.
253	   */
254	  review_on?: string;
255	
256	  /** Restricted-chart category; see `Restriction`. */
257	  restricted?: Restriction;
258	
259	  /** Visit the event was entered at; absent for phone refills and reconciliation outside a visit. */
260	  visit_id?: string;
261	}
262	
263	/**
264	 * One change to one line of the problem list. The problem list is maintained by hand: a line
265	 * changes only when a clinician edits it, so a line can be out of date with respect to newer
266	 * results or other organizations' diagnoses (see `ListReviewed` for why a review does not mean the
267	 * line is current).
268	 */
269	export interface ProblemEvent {
270	  type: 'problem_event';
271	
272	  /** Northgate problem-list line id, e.g. "PL-11902". Stable across all events for one line. */
273	  problem_id: string;
274	
275	  /**
276	   * What happened to the line.
277	   * - 'add': line created.
278	   * - 'update': description, codes or onset edited. Staging changes are made this way (the line
279	   *   keeps its id), so the latest 'update' carries the current wording.
280	   * - 'resolve': problem no longer active; the line moves to Past Medical History.
281	   * - 'remove': line deleted from the list because it was wrong (not because the problem resolved).
282	   */
283	  action: 'add' | 'update' | 'resolve' | 'remove';
284	
285	  /** Problem as displayed on the list, e.g. "Chronic kidney disease stage 3a". Restated on every event. */
286	  description: string;
287	
288	  /** ICD-10-CM code chosen when the line was created or last updated. */
289	  icd10cm: string;
290	
291	  /** SNOMED CT concept from Northgate's terminology service. Absent for lines created before 2020. */
292	  snomed?: string;
293	
294	  /** When the problem began, with precision. Often year-only for problems that predate Northgate. */
295	  onset?: FuzzyDate;
296	
297	  /** Restricted-chart category; see `Restriction`. */
298	  restricted?: Restriction;
299	
300	  /** Visit the event was entered at, if any. */
301	  visit_id?: string;
302	}
303	
304	/**
305	 * One change to one line of the allergy list. Northgate's allergy list holds allergies,
306	 * intolerances and adverse reactions in one list; `reaction_type` says which.
307	 */
308	export interface AllergyEvent {
309	  type: 'allergy_event';
310	
311	  /** Northgate allergy-list line id, e.g. "AL-2207". Stable across events for one line. */
312	  allergy_id: string;
313	
314	  /**
315	   * What happened to the line.
316	   * - 'add': line created.
317	   * - 'update': reaction, severity or comment edited.
318	   * - 'inactivate': no longer considered valid (e.g. patient tolerated a re-challenge). The line
319	   *   stays in history.
320	   */
321	  action: 'add' | 'update' | 'inactivate';
322	
323	  /**
324	   * The substance. `rxnorm` is an RxNorm ingredient CUI for drugs; absent for foods and
325	   * environmental allergens, which have `name` only.
326	   */
327	  substance: { name: string; rxnorm?: string };
328	
329	  /**
330	   * Kind of reaction, as chosen by the clinician.
331	   * - 'allergy': immune-mediated (hives, angioedema, anaphylaxis).
332	   * - 'intolerance': non-immune, predictable side effect that made the drug unacceptable (e.g.
333	   *   ACE-inhibitor cough). Not an allergy.
334	   * - 'adverse_reaction': a serious harmful event attributed to the drug that is not an allergy
335	   *   (e.g. drug-associated ketoacidosis).
336	   */
337	  reaction_type: 'allergy' | 'intolerance' | 'adverse_reaction';
338	
339	  /** Reactions from Northgate's picklist, display text, e.g. ["Cough"]. At least one. */
340	  reactions: string[];
341	
342	  /**
343	   * Northgate's "severity" field, which is really criticality: how dangerous re-exposure is
344	   * judged to be, not how bad the past reaction was.
345	   * - 'low': re-exposure unlikely to cause serious harm.
346	   * - 'high': re-exposure could be serious or life-threatening.
347	   * - 'unknown': not assessed.
348	   */
349	  severity: 'low' | 'high' | 'unknown';
350	
351	  /** When the reaction began, with precision. Absent if not recorded. */
352	  onset?: FuzzyDate;
353	
354	  /** Visit the event was entered at, if any. */
355	  visit_id?: string;
356	}
357	
358	/**
359	 * A clinician clicked "Mark as reviewed" on one of the patient's lists. Nothing on the list
360	 * changed. This records that the list was looked at, not that each line was re-confirmed: a
361	 * stale line stays stale after a review.
362	 */
363	export interface ListReviewed {
364	  type: 'list_reviewed';
365	
366	  /**
367	   * Which list was reviewed.
368	   * - 'problems', 'medications', 'allergies': the corresponding Northgate list.
369	   */
370	  list: 'problems' | 'medications' | 'allergies';
371	
372	  /** Line ids (`problem_id`, `med_id` or `allergy_id`) on the list at the time of the review, active and held lines included. */
373	  lines_on_list: string[];
374	
375	  /** Visit the review happened at. */
376	  visit_id?: string;
377	}
378	
379	/**
380	 * One result component received through Northgate's lab interface from Lakeview Labs and filed in
381	 * Northgate's chart. Northgate issues its own copy: the same result also exists in Lakeview's own
382	 * records under Lakeview's identifiers, and `external_ref` points to it. One item holds every
383	 * component from one Lakeview result report (accession).
384	 *
385	 * Values are filed as the interface delivered them, with two exceptions applied by Northgate's
386	 * interface translation table (see `unit`).
387	 *
388	 * Results of orders that Lakeview voided as entered in error are not sent over the interface, so they
389	 * never appear here.
390	 *
391	 * When Lakeview sends a correction for a report Northgate already filed, Northgate publishes a new
392	 * item that `supersedes` the old one and restates every component of the report as corrected, with
393	 * `result_status` 'C' on the components that changed. This includes a value the lab withdrew without
394	 * a replacement, as for a hemolyzed specimen: the corrected component then has a non-numeric `value`
395	 * (e.g. "Result invalidated") and the lab's explanation in `comment`. A separate redraw is a separate
396	 * accession and a separate item; it does not supersede anything.
397	 */
398	export interface ImportedResult {
399	  type: 'imported_result';
400	
401	  /**
402	   * The test.
403	   * - `nfm_code`: Northgate result-component code, e.g. "CREAT", "EGFR-NAA". Assigned by Northgate's
404	   *   interface mapping from Lakeview's code; stable across years except where Lakeview introduced
405	   *   a new test (see `external_ref.result_code`).
406	   * - `name`: Northgate display name.
407	   * - `loinc`: LOINC code, present only when Lakeview's message carried one. Lakeview leaves it
408	   *   off for several local tests, so do not rely on it to find a whole series.
409	   */
410	  test: { nfm_code: string; name: string; loinc?: string };
411	
412	  /**
413	   * Result value as text, exactly as received (HL7 OBX-5). Usually a plain number ("1.12"), but can
414	   * carry a comparator (">60", "<0.01") or be words ("Hemolyzed"). Numbers are never padded or
415	   * rounded by Northgate.
416	   */
417	  value: string;
418	
419	  /**
420	   * Unit text as filed. Not UCUM; examples: "mg/dL", "mL/min/1.73m2", "mmol/L", "mg/g", "%".
421	   * Empty string when the result has no unit.
422	   *
423	   * Northgate's interface translation table rewrites two analytes on the way in: platelet and
424	   * white-cell counts arrive from Lakeview in "K/uL" (thousands per microliter) and are filed
425	   * multiplied by 1000 in "cells/uL", reference range included. So a Lakeview platelet count of 212 K/uL
426	   * (range 150-450) is filed here as value "212000", unit "cells/uL", range "150000-450000". All other
427	   * analytes keep Lakeview's unit.
428	   */
429	  unit: string;
430	
431	  /** Reference range as text from the lab, e.g. "0.57-1.00" or ">59". Absent if none was sent. */
432	  reference_range?: string;
433	
434	  /**
435	   * Abnormal flag from the lab (HL7 OBX-8).
436	   * - 'H' / 'L': above / below the reference range.
437	   * - 'HH' / 'LL': critically high / low.
438	   * - 'A': abnormal, direction not given (non-numeric results).
439	   * Absent means the lab sent no flag (normal, or not flaggable).
440	   */
441	  flag?: 'H' | 'L' | 'HH' | 'LL' | 'A';
442	
443	  /**
444	   * Result status from the lab (HL7 OBX-11), as received.
445	   * - 'P': preliminary; a final will follow as a superseding item.
446	   * - 'F': final.
447	   * - 'C': corrected; this value replaces an earlier final for the same accession and component,
448	   *   and the item supersedes the Northgate item that held the earlier value. The corrected value can
449	   *   be non-numeric when the lab withdrew the result (see the interface comment).
450	   */
451	  result_status: 'P' | 'F' | 'C';
452	
453	  /** When the specimen was collected (HL7 OBR-7), with offset. The item's `effective` equals this. */
454	  collected: string;
455	
456	  /** When Lakeview released the result (HL7 OBX-14), with offset. The item's `recorded` is when Northgate filed it. */
457	  resulted: string;
458	
459	  /**
460	   * Lab comment attached to this component (HL7 NTE), verbatim. Lakeview uses it for method notes
461	   * (which eGFR equation) and specimen problems ("Specimen hemolyzed").
462	   */
463	  comment?: string;
464	
465	  /**
466	   * Where the result really comes from.
467	   * - `lab`: always "Lakeview Labs" in v1.
468	   * - `accession`: Lakeview's accession number; identical in Lakeview's own record of this result.
469	   * - `result_code`: Lakeview's own test code (e.g. "LK-CREAT", "LK-EGFR09N"). Lakeview retired
470	   *   its CKD-EPI 2009 eGFR codes on 2022-01-10 and introduced a race-free CKD-EPI 2021 code;
471	   *   Northgate maps each to its own `nfm_code`, so the eGFR series spans several codes.
472	   */
473	  external_ref: { lab: 'Lakeview Labs'; accession: string; result_code: string };
474	
475	  /** Northgate order number the result answers, e.g. "NO-2021-55120". Absent for results Lakeview sent without a Northgate order (standing orders). */
476	  order_id?: string;
477	}
478	
479	/**
480	 * One step of an outbound referral. Each step is its own event; the latest event per
481	 * `referral_id` gives the referral's current state.
482	 */
483	export interface ReferralEvent {
484	  type: 'referral_event';
485	
486	  /** Northgate referral number, e.g. "RF-2026-0884". */
487	  referral_id: string;
488	
489	  /**
490	   * What happened.
491	   * - 'created': referral written and sent; the item narrative is the referral letter if one was written.
492	   * - 'scheduled': the receiving organization booked an appointment.
493	   * - 'closed': consult note received or referral otherwise completed.
494	   * - 'cancelled': withdrawn.
495	   */
496	  action: 'created' | 'scheduled' | 'closed' | 'cancelled';
497	
498	  /** Receiving organization and specialty, display text, e.g. { org: "Lakeview Kidney Care", specialty: "Nephrology" }. */
499	  to: { org: string; specialty: string };
500	
501	  /** Clinical question as typed in the referral form. Restated on every event. */
502	  question: string;
503	
504	  /**
505	   * Urgency requested.
506	   * - 'routine': next available.
507	   * - 'urgent': within two weeks.
508	   */
509	  urgency: 'routine' | 'urgent';
510	
511	  /** Appointment date, on 'scheduled' only. Full date. */
512	  appointment_on?: string;
513	}
514	
515	/**
516	 * One diagnosis on a referral, chosen from the problem list when the referral was created. Each
517	 * referral step's item restates them, one entry per code, next to its `referral_event` entry.
518	 */
519	export interface ReferralDx {
520	  type: 'referral_dx';
521	
522	  /** The referral (the `referral_event` entry in the same item). */
523	  referral_id: string;
524	
525	  /** ICD-10-CM code, with the dot. */
526	  icd10cm: string;
527	
528	  /** Display text as on the problem list. */
529	  display: string;
530	
531	  /** Restricted-chart category; see `Restriction`. */
532	  restricted?: Restriction;
533	}
534	
535	/**
536	 * A void: one or more earlier Northgate items were entered in error and are withdrawn without
537	 * replacement. Voids are only for entries that should never have existed; a lab correction is a
538	 * superseding `ImportedResult` item, not a void. The void item's `effective` is the time of the void
539	 * and equals its `recorded`. The envelope `retracts` lists the same item ids as `voided_items`; this
540	 * entry adds Northgate's own reason code. The voided items stay in the log for audit.
541	 */
542	export interface ChartCorrection {
543	  type: 'chart_correction';
544	
545	  /** Ids of the Northgate items voided. Always identical to the envelope's `retracts`. */
546	  voided_items: string[];
547	
548	  /**
549	   * Why the items were voided.
550	   * - 'wrong_patient': entered on this patient's chart but meant for someone else. The voided
551	   *   content says nothing about this patient.
552	   * - 'entry_error': wrong value, wrong drug or similar typing mistake on the right patient.
553	   * - 'duplicate': the same event was entered twice; another item still records it.
554	   */
555	  reason: 'wrong_patient' | 'entry_error' | 'duplicate';
556	}

1	/**
2	 * Consumer views, version 1: the small shapes a patient-facing chart app reads.
3	 *
4	 * These are defined by the consumer, not by any source. A mapper turns one source's FOLIO record items
5	 * for one patient into these rows. The consumer merges rows from several sources itself, so a mapper
6	 * reports only what its own source says, and never invents, infers from other sources, or "corrects"
7	 * what the source records.
8	 *
9	 * Contract (see `Transform`): the mapper receives every item one source published for one patient,
10	 * in no particular order and including items that were later superseded or retracted, plus an
11	 * `asOf` date. It returns the rows that describe that source's record as it stood at the end of that
12	 * date.
13	 *
14	 * Conventions for every view:
15	 *
16	 * - **Scope in time.** An item is in scope when its envelope `recorded` time is on or before the end of
17	 *   the `asOf` day in America/Chicago. Ignore items recorded later. Apply the FOLIO correction rules to
18	 *   the items in scope: an item listed in another in-scope item's `supersedes` or `retracts` (same
19	 *   issuer) is not current; supersession is transitive. Use only current items, except where a view
20	 *   below says otherwise.
21	 * - **Time zone.** The consumer displays everything in America/Chicago. "Local date" and "local time"
22	 *   below mean wall-clock date/time in America/Chicago (UTC-6 standard, UTC-5 daylight time).
23	 * - **Partial dates.** `PartialDate` strings keep the precision the source actually knows: "2016"
24	 *   means some time in 2016, never 2016-01-01. Never pad a year-only or month-only date.
25	 * - **Only what the source records.** Rows come from structured payload entries. Narrative text may be
26	 *   used to understand an entry but must not be the only basis for a row.
27	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and payload entry ids) it was built from, so the consumer
28	 *   can show the source text behind a fact.
29	 * - **Determinism.** Same input, same output: no clock, randomness, network or file access.
30	 */
31	
32	/** A FOLIO record item in its JSON form (see the FOLIO record-item spec). */
33	export interface FolioItem {
34	  folio: string;
35	  /** Item id (ULID), unique within the issuer. */
36	  id: string;
37	  /** did:web of the issuing organization. */
38	  issuer: string;
39	  /** Patient id at this issuer. */
40	  patient: string;
41	  /** When the clinical event happened: RFC 3339 date-time with offset, or a full or partial date. */
42	  effective: string;
43	  effective_end?: string;
44	  /** When the issuer committed this item: RFC 3339 date-time with offset. */
45	  recorded: string;
46	  author?: { id?: string; name?: string; role?: string };
47	  /** The payload's schema: `type` names the entry type in the source's .d.ts. */
48	  schema?: { url: string; type: string; sha256: string };
49	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that this item replaces entirely. */
50	  supersedes?: string[];
51	  /** Ids of earlier items from the same issuer that were entered in error, withdrawn without replacement. */
52	  retracts?: string[];
53	  /** Markdown narrative with `<ref id="…">…</ref>` spans; "" if none. */
54	  narrative: string;
55	  /** Entry id -> entry, each entry typed by the source's schema; {} if none. */
56	  payload: Record<string, any>;
57	}
58	
59	/** The mapper's entry point. `asOf` is a local date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. */
60	export type Transform = (items: FolioItem[], asOf: string) => ViewRows;
61	
62	/** Everything one mapper returns for one patient and one source. Empty arrays where the source has nothing. */
63	export interface ViewRows {
64	  medications: MedicationRow[];
65	  problems: ProblemRow[];
66	  allergies: AllergyIntoleranceRow[];
67	  labs: LabResultRow[];
68	  vitals: VitalRow[];
69	}
70	
71	/** `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD`; the precision is the string's length. */
72	export type PartialDate = string;
73	
74	/** The items (and entries inside them) a row was built from. At least one. */
75	export type Evidence = { item_id: string; entry_id?: string }[];
76	
77	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
78	// Medications
79	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
80	
81	/**
82	 * One outpatient (home) medication as this source records it, with its status as of `asOf`.
83	 *
84	 * - One row per drug ingredient. If the source has several lines, orders or prescriptions for the
85	 *   same ingredient over time (stopped and restarted, re-entered), report the most recent one, i.e.
86	 *   the one whose own latest event is latest. A line or order that was entered in error, voided or
87	 *   retracted never existed: do not report it, and do not let it affect another line.
88	 * - Include medications that are stopped (status 'stopped') if the source still shows them, so the
89	 *   consumer can say what was stopped and why.
90	 * - Exclude hospital-only orders (infusions, IV fluids, inpatient-only drugs). They are not home
91	 *   medications.
92	 * - When the source publishes a medication list as repeated snapshots (each document or save restates
93	 *   the list), the latest in-scope snapshot is the source's list; a drug missing from the latest
94	 *   snapshot is not reported. When the source publishes events or status rows, the latest event or
95	 *   status row for a line determines its state, however old it is.
96	 */
97	export interface MedicationRow {
98	  /**
99	   * Generic ingredient name, lower case, without salt or form: "losartan" (not "losartan potassium"),
100	   * "metformin", "insulin glargine", "empagliflozin". Translate brand names the record uses
101	   * ("Jardiance" -> "empagliflozin"). Omit only when the record does not say which drug it is (e.g. the
102	   * patient wrote "water pill").
103	   */
104	  ingredient?: string;
105	  /** RxNorm ingredient CUI, only when the source states an ingredient-level RxNorm code. Never guessed or derived from a product code. */
106	  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
107	  /** The drug as the source names it (display text), e.g. "losartan potassium 50 MG Oral Tablet" or "Jardiance". */
108	  drug_name: string;
109	  /**
110	   * Status as of `asOf`, by this source's account.
111	   * - 'active': the patient should be taking it (or, on a patient's own list, says they are).
112	   * - 'held': paused with intent (or at least possibility) of resuming; the patient should not be
113	   *   taking it now. Not the same as stopped.
114	   * - 'stopped': discontinued.
115	   * - 'unknown': the source lists the drug but records no decision about whether it is being taken
116	   *   (e.g. a hospital list marked as not reconciled).
117	   */
118	  status: 'active' | 'held' | 'stopped' | 'unknown';
119	  /**
120	   * Local date on which the current status began according to this source: for 'held' or 'stopped',
121	   * the date of the hold or stop; for 'active', the date the source's current line or order started
122	   * (or resumed). Keep the source's precision. Omit if the source does not say.
123	   */
124	  status_since?: PartialDate;
125	  /**
126	   * Amount per administration currently prescribed (for 'held' and 'stopped': the amount when it was
127	   * held or stopped). For a patient's own list: the amount the patient says they take, if they give
128	   * one. `unit` is one of the listed units; convert source spellings ("unit", "UNT", "[iU]" ->
129	   * "units"; "tab"/"tablets" -> "tablet"). Omit when the source gives no single amount.
130	   */
131	  dose?: { value: number; unit: 'mg' | 'mcg' | 'units' | 'mL' | 'tablet' };
132	  /**
133	   * How often, normalized: 'QD' once daily, 'BID' twice daily, 'TID' three times daily, 'QHS' once
134	   * daily at bedtime, 'QW' once weekly, 'PRN' as needed, 'other' anything else. Omit if unknown.
135	   */
136	  frequency?: 'QD' | 'BID' | 'TID' | 'QHS' | 'QW' | 'PRN' | 'other';
137	  /**
138	   * For 'stopped' rows, why, when the source records a coded or clearly stated reason:
139	   * - 'adverse_reaction': side effect or adverse reaction.
140	   * - 'ineffective': not working well enough.
141	   * - 'therapy_changed': replaced by another drug for the same purpose.
142	   * - 'course_complete': finite course finished.
143	   * - 'patient_choice': the patient declined or asked to stop.
144	   * - 'other': another reason (see `status_reason_text`).
145	   * Omit when the source gives no reason, and on rows that are not 'stopped'.
146	   */
147	  stop_reason?: 'adverse_reaction' | 'ineffective' | 'therapy_changed' | 'course_complete' | 'patient_choice' | 'other';
148	  /** Free-text reason for the current status (hold or stop) as the source wrote it, if any. */
149	  status_reason_text?: string;
150	  /** True when the row comes from the patient's own account (a self-reported list), not a clinician's record. */
151	  patient_reported: boolean;
152	  /** True when the source says the drug was bought without a prescription. Omit otherwise. */
153	  otc?: boolean;
154	  evidence: Evidence;
155	}
156	
157	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
158	// Problems
159	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
160	
161	/**
162	 * One condition on the source's problem list (or the source's equivalent: its diagnosis or history
163	 * lists), with status as of `asOf`.
164	 *
165	 * - One row per condition. Several entries for the same condition (re-listed in several documents,
166	 *   restaged, re-coded) are one row whose fields reflect the latest entry.
167	 * - Report only conditions the source asserts the patient has or had. Never report a condition that
168	 *   was ruled out, or one that was only suspected (working/provisional) and never confirmed.
169	 * - Billing codes attached to a visit or claim are not problem-list entries, unless the source says
170	 *   its problem list is built from them.
171	 * - An adverse effect of a drug (however the source records it, including as an ICD-10 T-code
172	 *   diagnosis) is an `AllergyIntoleranceRow` of type 'adverse_reaction', not a problem. The illness it
173	 *   caused (e.g. ketoacidosis) is still a problem.
174	 */
175	export interface ProblemRow {
176	  /** The condition as the source words it, e.g. "Chronic kidney disease stage 3a". */
177	  condition: string;
178	  /** ICD-10-CM code, with the dot, as the source gives it (latest). Omit if the source gives none. */
179	  icd10cm?: string;
180	  /** SNOMED CT concept id, if the source gives one. */
181	  snomed?: string;
182	  /**
183	   * - 'active': the patient has it.
184	   * - 'resolved': the patient had it and the source says it is resolved or historical.
185	   */
186	  status: 'active' | 'resolved';
187	  /** When the condition began, at the precision the source knows. Omit if the source does not say. */
188	  onset?: { value: PartialDate; precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day' };
189	  /**
190	   * For chronic kidney disease only: the KDIGO GFR category the source most recently recorded for this
191	   * patient ('G3a' for "stage 3a", "N18.31" or a G3a category field). As recorded by a clinician; never
192	   * computed from lab values.
193	   */
194	  ckd_stage?: 'G1' | 'G2' | 'G3a' | 'G3b' | 'G4' | 'G5';
195	  /** For chronic kidney disease only: KDIGO albuminuria category as recorded ('A1', 'A2', 'A3'), if the source records one. */
196	  albuminuria?: 'A1' | 'A2' | 'A3';
197	  evidence: Evidence;
198	}
199	
200	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
201	// Allergies, intolerances, adverse reactions
202	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
203	
204	/**
205	 * One substance the patient should avoid or be careful with, as of `asOf`. Only current entries: an
206	 * entry the source marks inactive or invalid is not reported. "No known drug allergies" is not a row.
207	 */
208	export interface AllergyIntoleranceRow {
209	  /** Substance: generic ingredient name, lower case, for drugs ("lisinopril"); as written otherwise. */
210	  substance: string;
211	  /** RxNorm ingredient CUI, if the source gives one. */
212	  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
213	  /**
214	   * What kind of reaction, by its nature (not by which list the source keeps it on):
215	   * - 'allergy': immune-mediated (hives, rash, angioedema, anaphylaxis, bronchospasm).
216	   * - 'intolerance': a non-immune, predictable side effect that made the drug unacceptable (e.g.
217	   *   ACE-inhibitor cough, GI upset).
218	   * - 'adverse_reaction': a serious harmful event attributed to the drug that is not an allergy (e.g.
219	   *   drug-associated ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis).
220	   * If the source keeps all three on one undifferentiated list, decide from the recorded reaction.
221	   */
222	  type: 'allergy' | 'intolerance' | 'adverse_reaction';
223	  /** Reaction(s) as the source words them, joined with "; ". Omit if not recorded. */
224	  reaction?: string;
225	  /**
226	   * Criticality: how dangerous re-exposure is judged to be.
227	   * - 'high': re-exposure could be serious or life-threatening.
228	   * - 'low': re-exposure unlikely to cause serious harm.
229	   * - 'unknown': not assessed or not derivable.
230	   * A source's "severity" scale is mapped by meaning: mild -> 'low'; severe or life-threatening -> 'high'.
231	   */
232	  criticality: 'low' | 'high' | 'unknown';
233	  /** When the reaction began, at the precision the source knows. */
234	  onset?: { value: PartialDate; precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day' };
235	  evidence: Evidence;
236	}
237	
238	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
239	// Lab results
240	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
241	
242	/**
243	 * Analytes this consumer tracks, with the unit `LabResultRow.value` must be in. Results for other
244	 * tests are not reported.
245	 *
246	 * | analyte         | unit            | notes |
247	 * |-----------------|-----------------|-------|
248	 * | creatinine      | mg/dL           | serum |
249	 * | egfr            | mL/min/1.73m2   | see `egfr_equation` and the eGFR rule below |
250	 * | potassium       | mmol/L          | |
251	 * | sodium          | mmol/L          | |
252	 * | chloride        | mmol/L          | |
253	 * | bicarbonate     | mmol/L          | total CO2 |
254	 * | anion_gap       | mmol/L          | |
255	 * | bun             | mg/dL           | urea nitrogen |
256	 * | glucose         | mg/dL           | laboratory glucose (serum/plasma); home meter readings are vitals |
257	 * | a1c             | %               | NGSP |
258	 * | uacr            | mg/g            | urine albumin/creatinine ratio |
259	 * | platelets       | 10*3/uL         | thousands per microlitre: 212 000 cells/uL is 212 |
260	 * | wbc             | 10*3/uL         | thousands per microlitre |
261	 * | hemoglobin      | g/dL            | |
262	 * | bhb             | mmol/L          | beta-hydroxybutyrate |
263	 * | ph              | [pH]            | blood gas pH |
264	 * | pco2            | mmHg            | |
265	 * | lipase          | U/L             | |
266	 * | troponin        | ng/mL           | troponin I |
267	 * | cholesterol     | mg/dL           | total |
268	 * | triglycerides   | mg/dL           | |
269	 * | hdl             | mg/dL           | |
270	 * | ldl             | mg/dL           | measured or calculated |
271	 */
272	export type Analyte =
273	  | 'creatinine' | 'egfr' | 'potassium' | 'sodium' | 'chloride' | 'bicarbonate' | 'anion_gap' | 'bun'
274	  | 'glucose' | 'a1c' | 'uacr' | 'platelets' | 'wbc' | 'hemoglobin' | 'bhb' | 'ph' | 'pco2' | 'lipase'
275	  | 'troponin' | 'cholesterol' | 'triglycerides' | 'hdl' | 'ldl';
276	
277	/**
278	 * One valid laboratory result.
279	 *
280	 * - One row per result. A result the source shows several times (copies in several documents, a
281	 *   preliminary and a final copy) is one row, taken from the copy with the most advanced status.
282	 * - Report only values that stand: leave out results that were withdrawn, invalidated or "corrected
283	 *   away" by the lab, results of orders voided or entered in error, results not performed, and
284	 *   superseded copies. A confirmation repeat is a second valid result; keep both.
285	 * - **eGFR rule.** One eGFR row per eGFR calculation the source reports for a specimen. When the source
286	 *   reports race-specific variants of one calculation (a value with and one without a race
287	 *   coefficient), report only the variant without the race coefficient. Report the value as printed
288	 *   (do not recompute).
289	 */
290	export interface LabResultRow {
291	  analyte: Analyte;
292	  /** Numeric value in the analyte's unit (see `Analyte`). For a result printed with a comparator (">60", "<0.01"), the number part. */
293	  value: number;
294	  /** Set when the printed result has a comparator: ">60" -> value 60, comparator '>'. */
295	  comparator?: '<' | '>' | '<=' | '>=';
296	  /** The analyte's unit from the table in `Analyte`, exactly as written there. */
297	  unit: string;
298	  /** Specimen collection time, RFC 3339 with offset (any offset; it denotes an instant). */
299	  collected: string;
300	  /** 'final' (also for amended or corrected values that stand) or 'preliminary'. */
301	  status: 'final' | 'preliminary';
302	  /**
303	   * For analyte 'egfr' only: the equation the source says it used.
304	   * - 'ckd-epi-2021': CKD-EPI 2021 (race-free).
305	   * - 'ckd-epi-2009': CKD-EPI 2009.
306	   * - 'mdrd': MDRD.
307	   * - 'unknown': not stated.
308	   * When a code and a method note disagree, believe the method note.
309	   */
310	  egfr_equation?: 'ckd-epi-2021' | 'ckd-epi-2009' | 'mdrd' | 'unknown';
311	  /** LOINC code if the source gives one for this result. */
312	  loinc?: string;
313	  evidence: Evidence;
314	}
315	
316	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
317	// Vital signs and home readings
318	// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
319	
320	/**
321	 * One set of vital signs taken together, or one home reading.
322	 *
323	 * - A clinic or hospital vital-sign set (BP, pulse, weight taken within a few minutes at one visit) is
324	 *   one row; `local_time` is the time of its first blood pressure (or of its first measurement if no
325	 *   BP). A repeat blood pressure taken later in the same visit goes in `repeat_*` on the same row.
326	 * - Each home BP reading and each home glucose reading is its own row.
327	 * - Each measurement is reported once: if a source shows the same measurement twice (a reading typed
328	 *   in by hand that duplicates one synced from the device a minute or two earlier with the same
329	 *   values), report it once, preferring the device copy.
330	 */
331	export interface VitalRow {
332	  /** 'clinic' (outpatient office), 'hospital' (ED or inpatient), or 'home' (patient's own devices). */
333	  setting: 'clinic' | 'hospital' | 'home';
334	  /** Local wall-clock time in America/Chicago, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM`. */
335	  local_time: string;
336	  systolic_mmhg?: number;
337	  diastolic_mmhg?: number;
338	  /** Repeat blood pressure at the same visit, if one was taken. */
339	  repeat_systolic_mmhg?: number;
340	  repeat_diastolic_mmhg?: number;
341	  pulse_bpm?: number;
342	  /** Body weight in kilograms (1 lb = 0.45359237 kg), one decimal place. */
343	  weight_kg?: number;
344	  /** Home glucose meter reading in mg/dL (1 mmol/L = 18.016 mg/dL), rounded to a whole number. */
345	  glucose_mg_dl?: number;
346	  /** Set when the meter showed HI or LO instead of a number; `glucose_mg_dl` is then the meter's limit in mg/dL. */
347	  glucose_out_of_range?: 'HI' | 'LO';
348	  evidence: Evidence;
349	}

I revised `out/transform.ts` with one change: a medication line whose frequency is `OTHER` or missing, and whose `sig` says "weekly" or "once a week", now gets frequency `QW`. I didn't run the revised mapper against the feedback patients, so the weekly-dulaglutide case isn't checked directly. It type-checks and runs on the sample patients. The feedback listed 9 discrepancies, and I treated the other 8 as the reader's errors:

- **eGFR values off by 1–3 (49 vs 47, 46, 57 vs 56, 44 vs 43):** the mapper reports the structured lab value as printed, and the narratives look like clinician approximations. For the 2020 case (49 vs 47), the 49 may be the race-coefficient variant. The views' eGFR rule says to drop that variant and keep the one without.
- **A1c, UACR and eGFR that appear only in narrative or `reason_text`:** these are not payload `imported_result` entries, and the views say a row can't rest on narrative alone, so I emit no lab row.
- **Behavioral-health depression problem (`restricted: "BH"`):** I still leave it out. The schema says restricted entries are excluded from routine outbound records unless the patient consents, and the data carries no consent. This is a judgment call: if consent should be assumed, restricted problems would need to be included.
